Four Knots, One Corner

SSF-MS8-L2-300650-MSMATH8-DBT-GBL
THE DIRECTIONS
You will talk to four people. Record what you would say to each one. You can record again as many times as you want. When all four are recorded, click Submit.
The first time you press record, your computer will ask to use your microphone. Click Allow.
The park map
As you record, the four lengths fill in. Test the corner first, then find the new path.

THE SCENE
You are in a debate with a school in another country. Your side wants the city to build a new path in the park. Two park paths meet at a corner. One goes to the tree. The other goes to the gate, past the bench. The new path would run straight from the tree to the bench. You must show the corner is a square corner. Then give the length of the new path. Four people each have one length you need.
THE HISTORY
Builders long ago used a rope to make square corners. The rope had knots at 3, 4, and 5 steps. India, China, and Babylon all wrote down the same rule. Greece named the rule after Pythagoras.
